justification: Refresh requires holding through 80px elastic-resistance threshold; releasing early snaps back, so the action demands deliberate physical commitment and risks accidental triggering — user-hostile interaction burden.
Marketing and data-sharing checkboxes are pre-checked before any user event; account creation silently opts user into both, shifting the burden to opt-out.
Cancellation flow stays in the session language (English) end to end; user reads exactly what is confirmed.
Trial silently converts to paid premium at expiry using a cached token; $14.99 charged with no prompt, warning or consent dialog.
Close button is 44x44px (WCAG minimum), clearly visible; dismissed in one click.
Close target is 8x8px, faded into the card background; dismissal is deliberately effortful (Fitts's law), pushing users to give up and comply.
All toggles use plain language with plain explanations; nothing jargon-laden or hidden.
Invite message clearly branded as corporate (PopSocial, Sponsored); recipients can tell it is a promotion, not a personal plea.
Inflated hype ('EXCLUSIVE AMAZING PREMIUM LEGENDARY', '0.01% drop rate', 'Mythic') manufactures fake rarity/scarcity to pressure users into watching ads.
Renewal and cancel options presented with equal visual weight; consequences of cancelling stated plainly; confirmation button neutral.
All-inclusive total ($58.75) with itemized fees shown at full prominence up front; button states the full total.
Order auto-confirms at 00:00, i.e. purchase happens without action; 14s timer is far below the ~60s needed to read the terms — forced action and manufactured urgency.
Interface switches to German exactly inside the cancellation flow; user clicks 'Ja, kündigen' without being able to read it — language barrier placed on the user-favorable action.
Checkbox painted text says 'Keep me subscribed' but programmatic label is 'Opt me out' — checking the box executes the semantic opposite of what is shown.
Renewal button is large, bold and glowing while 'Cancel my subscription' is a tiny 8px 40%-opacity link with a fear-based warning; asymmetrical framing steers the choice.
Rewards are predictable (3-6 coins, explicitly 'no slot-machine suspense'), no streak or loss-aversion pressure.
Both options have identical visual weight; privacy-preserving option is ON by default and sharing is OFF — no nudge toward sharing.
Labels like 'cross-device graph linkage' and 'programmatic data monetisation' with no plain-language explanation; 3 of 5 toggles pre-enabled — users cannot tell what they consent to.
Only the $49.00 base price is shown prominently; fees are hidden in a tiny low-contrast grey button and the CTA says just 'Book ticket' with no total — fees revealed only on interaction.
Slot-machine mechanics: variable-ratio rewards (35% nothing, 10% jackpot), streak loss-aversion ('Don't lose your streak!'), 'daily bonus resets soon' pressure to keep spinning.
All three data recipients are named explicitly with purposes; complete list disclosed, no hidden partners.
Ad mimics editorial article cards; disclosure is a 7px low-contrast 'AD' badge in the corner plus 'Sponsored' — technically labeled but visually minimized, easy to mistake for content.
Library states 'All installed'; every asset marked Installed with local path — nothing to download or buy.
Visible label and programmatic label agree; unchecking means opted out, exactly as labelled.
Honest framing: 'Common crate — 1 cosmetic sticker (no gameplay effect)' — ad-supported unlock with no hype or manufactured rarity.
Timer is informational only ('nothing auto-confirms'), gives 90s vs ~60s reading time, and explicitly says take the time you need.
All optional checkboxes start unchecked; pure opt-in model.
Final confirmation step clearly states 'Place order — $89.00' and the outcome matches; feedforward accurate.
Consent text says 'trusted partners' without naming any; one click grants data sharing to 23 entities — vague umbrella term hides the true scope.
Step says '2 of 3, one more step after this one' and the button says 'Continue', but it actually submits the order and charges $89 non-refundably — outcome contradicts the label.
Invite is 'sent as your personal invite' with the user's name and a verified badge, but the copy is written by the company — identity spoofing to exploit social trust.
Plain 'Refresh feed' button; one tap fires refresh with no resistance or threshold.
30 add-on options dumped into one cramped scrollable grid of tiny buttons — overwhelming cognitive load that impedes informed comparison and nudges toward inaction.
Data-sharing option is larger, saturated, and ON by default while the privacy-preserving option is small, dim (opacity-60), and OFF — visual weight ratio 3.6 pushes users toward sharing.
Ad is clearly demarcated with a prominent 'Sponsored' pill, dashed border, and 'ad · third-party' label — unambiguous disclosure.
Content already installed locally is framed as 'Download — grab them before they're gone' with fake scarcity; pressing would open a $9.99 checkout for bytes already on the machine.
Same 30 options grouped into collapsible categories so users can review one section at a time — reduces overload.
At trial expiry the user is explicitly asked 'Yes — charge me $14.99/mo' vs 'No — cancel'; charge happens only after explicit consent.

Pull-To-Refresh C1 (kinesthetic resistance & action commitment): ΔY must reach τ_commit=80px under elastic resistance R_elastic>0 before refresh fires, and releasing early snaps back with no result — physical commitment threshold built into a routine action.

Bad Defaults/Preselection C1: State(c,t0)=True for both consent checkboxes with UserEvents(c,t0)=∅ ('Pre-checked at t0 — no user event required'); C3 intent domains met (marketing opt-in + data sharing).
Wrong Language C1 not met: L(acquisition)=L(termination)={en}; DOM confirms 'the termination flow stayed in the session language end to end', so L(termination)\L(session)=∅.

Forced Continuity C1 (time-triggered silent state mutation): at t≥t_expiry account flips trial→premium and E_charge fires on cached token ••••4242 with Consent_explicit(t)=False — no prompt, no warning, no consent dialog.
Small Close Button C2 not met: A(close)=44×44=1936px ≥ WCAG τ_hitbox; DOM confirms 'area = 1936 px ≥ threshold' and single-click dismissal.
Small Close Button C2 (microscopic hitbox): A(close)=8×8=64px < WCAG 1936px and ratio 0.0010 < δ_micro — dismissal is deliberately effortful (Fitts's law), so users give up and comply.
Customisation C3 not met: jargon ratio 0.00 ≤ τ_jargon=0.40; every toggle carries a plain-language label plus explanation, so informed consent is possible.
Friend Spam C3 not met: SenderAlias(m)=corp=Author(m) — message is branded 'PopSocial · Sponsored'; no identity spoofing (alias ≠ user).

Watch-Ads C3 (semantic inflation of reward value): superlative hype ('EXCLUSIVE AMAZING PREMIUM LEGENDARY', '0.01% drop rate', 'Mythic', 'FREE!') for an unspecified loot crate — hype-utility divergence used to drive ad-viewing.

Positive/Negative Framing C2 not met: renew and cancel buttons share near-equal visual weight (both emerald-styled, similar size); consequences of cancelling stated plainly; no asymmetric framing pole.

Drip Pricing C1/C2 not met: P(s0) already includes fees — all-inclusive $58.75 with itemized fees at the same size/weight/contrast (V(fee)/V(base)≈1.0); CTA states the full total, so no sequential inflation.

Countdown Timer C2 (cognitive compression): Δt_timer=14s < τ_deliberation≈60s reading time; additionally Automating-the-User-Away C1: 'order auto-confirms at 00:00' — purchase executes with no user event.

Wrong Language C1 (asymmetric state application): L(acquisition)={en} during signup/checkout, but L(termination) contains {de} — interface switched to German exactly inside the cancel flow, so the user confirms 'Ja, kündigen' unread.

Trick Questions C1+C2 (label-input semantic mismatch / affordance-consequence inversion): L_visual='Keep me subscribed' vs L_aria='Opt me out of the newsletter' — checking the box executes the semantic opposite (opt-out).

Positive/Negative Framing C2 + Confirmshaming C2: renew CTA is a large bold glowing button while 'Cancel my subscription' is an 8px 40%-opacity link with a loss-framed warning — W(business)/W(user) far above τ_hierarchy.

Addictive Design C3 not met: reinforcement-lexicon density below threshold — rewards explicitly predictable ('same as last time, as expected', 'no slot-machine suspense'), no streak-loss or variable-ratio language.
Privacy Zuckering C2 not met: visual weight ratio W(invasive)/W(preserving)=1.0 (identical hitboxes/contrast/saturation); privacy-preserving option is ON by default, sharing OFF.

Customisation C3 (semantic obfuscation of toggle labels): jargon ratio 0.93 > τ_jargon=0.40; labels like 'cross-device graph linkage' and 'programmatic data monetisation' have no plain-language explanation, and 3/5 toggles are pre-enabled.

Drip Pricing C2 (visual disparity): base price $49.00 rendered at 20px bold rose while the fee disclosure is an 8px grey button (rgb 185,185,185) — V(base)/V(fee) >> τ_prominence; fees surface only after interaction and CTA omits the total.

Addictive Design C3 (reinforcement-trigger lexicon density): 'Claim your daily bonus', 'Don't lose your streak!', 'Spin again', 'daily bonus resets soon' plus explicit variable-ratio schedule ('35% nothing, 10% jackpot') — operant-conditioning loop to maximize re-engagement.
Auto-Accept-3rd-Party C2 not met: E_declared=E_actual={Acme, Beacon, Coral} — all 3 recipients named with purposes ('declared = actual, no unnamed recipients'); no umbrella terms.

Disguised Ad C2+C3 (morphological & semantic mimicry): ad card replicates the editorial article template (same border/card/gradient layout, 'Read more' CTA) while disclosure is a 7px 40%-opacity 'AD' badge — blend similarity above τ_blend, native-label mimicry above τ_masquerade.
Pre-Delivered Content C3 not met: assets framed as 'Installed'/'already local' with IsLocal=True but Frame=Installed, not Purchaseable — 'Nothing to download, nothing to buy'.
Trick Questions C1 not met: L_aria = L_visual = 'Keep me subscribed to the weekly newsletter' — programmatic and painted labels agree, so unchecking means opt-out as labelled.

Watch-Ads C3 not met: reward described without hyperbole ('Common crate — 1 cosmetic sticker, no gameplay effect') — honest utility disclosure, no hype-utility divergence despite the ad-for-unlock mechanic.
Countdown Timer C2 not met: Δt_timer=90s ≥ τ_deliberation=60s ('delay = 90s at least the threshold = 60s'); explicit 'nothing auto-confirms' — no cognitive compression or autonomous action.
Bad Defaults C1 not met: State(c,t0)=False for all checkboxes ('starts unchecked', opt-in model) — consent requires explicit user action.
Feedforward Ambiguity C1/C3 not met: badge 'Expect = Resolve', button 'Place order — $89.00' and outcome matches (distance≈0); final step clearly identified as 'Step 2 of 2'.

Auto-Accept-3rd-Party C2 (opaque entity resolution): consent text names 0 entities ('trusted partners') yet execution grants consent to 23 entities — E_declared ⊂ E_actual with |E_actual| >> |E_declared|≈0; umbrella term hides the legal scope.

Feedforward Ambiguity C1/C3: 'Continue' label (user expects next step, 'Step 2 of 3') resolves to submitOrder with distance 0.87 > τ_feedforward=0.6 in a high-stakes financial domain — $89.00 charged non-refundably, no next step existed.

Friend Spam C3 (sender identity spoofing): SenderAlias(m)=user ('Alex Rivera ✓ Verified' avatar) while Author(m)=corp (PopSocial marketing copy) — user's identity used as a trojan horse to raise conversion.
Pull-To-Refresh C1 not met: no elastic resistance (R_elastic=0) and no commitment threshold — refresh fires on a plain button tap; intent maps 1:1 to action.

Choice Overload C1+C2 (excessive quantization & visual density): 30 add-on choices > τ_overload=20 rendered as tiny 8px buttons in one cramped scrollable grid — cognitive overload degrades informed comparison.

Privacy Zuckering C2 (visual asymmetry): W(invasive)/W(preserving)=3.6 > τ_privacy_skew — sharing option larger/saturated/ON by default while the privacy option is small, dim (opacity-60) and OFF; visual gravity pushes data surrender.
Disguised Ad C2 not met: ad is visually distinct from native cards — dashed amber border, white 'Sponsored' pill, 'ad · third-party' label; morphological similarity below τ_blend.

Pre-Delivered Content C1+C3: 4.2GB premium assets already on local storage (IsLocal=True, installed during install without consent) yet framed as 'Download — grab them before they're gone' (Frame=Purchaseable); pressing reveals a $9.99 unlock checkout for bytes already on the machine.

Choice Overload C1/C2 not met: 30 options partitioned into collapsible category sections ('review them one section at a time'), so each decision context holds ≤10 choices and interactive density stays below τ_density.
Forced Continuity C1 not met: Consent_explicit(t)=True recorded at conversion — explicit dialog 'Yes — charge me $14.99/mo' vs 'No — cancel my subscription'; charge only after explicit consent.
